H_hierarchical.evidence: Figure 5 presents a flat flow among Follow/Check lane states and STOP; no parent state, nested mode, or composite sub-FSM is described.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions depend on measured obstacle distance and vehicle orientation; orientation is computed from wheel travel using q(k+1)=q(k)+(DDR(k)-DDL(k))/L and compared against turning thresholds.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Each state has code to keep lane or turn, while continuously monitoring obstacles; outputs include motor PWM and ultrasonic-sensor servo heading, with PID and bounded proportional controllers.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper includes a STOP terminal state but does not define faults, recovery transitions, rollback, or from-any-state emergency handling.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State names are in Figure 5, guard/action prose appears in Sections 2.2 and 3.1, and arithmetic control details appear later in Section 2.4.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as lane following, obstacle detected, and lane free are accompanied by explicit sensor thresholds and lane assumptions rather than relying mainly on outside domain decoding.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The state list does not co-locate actions; actions such as following road, turning, PWM output, and servo heading are described in separate narrative sections.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: Transition guards use distance and orientation; orientation is derived arithmetically from right/left wheel distances before threshold-based lane-change stopping.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite state has its own entry, during, or exit behavior beyond substates.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No global from-any-state fault or recovery rule is declared.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no composite-state initialization or pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: Distance and orientation guards involve arithmetic/comparison logic, but the paper does not expose three or more rich boolean-arithmetic guard formulas.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Obstacle monitoring is repeated conceptually, but no parent-level during action or uniform cross-cutting forced transition applies to three or more substates.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are concrete motor PWM and ultrasonic servo commands, not effector-agnostic logging, publishing, or notification actions.

key_nl_quotes: Each state has code to either keep the current lane or to turn in order to change lane, depending on the distance measured by the nearest obstacle ahead.
The transition between states happens because of guard conditions on the measured distance and on the orientation of the vehicle with respect to the direction of the road.
one_line_pitch: A flat but action-heavy Stateflow WMR controller whose guard/action semantics are scattered across figures, prose, and control equations.
rationale: This is a meaningful guard-and-action stress case: the paper ties lane transitions to obstacle distance, estimated orientation, PID lane following, bounded turning, PWM motor outputs, and servo heading. It is not a top candidate because it lacks hierarchy and a real fault-recovery model, so it mainly stresses guard extraction and action attribution rather than the full weak surface of the baseline.
